\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چادر} (châdor)}{چادر (châdor)}]{\fa{چادر} (châdor) — a tent; a chador (a woman's full cloak)}

\label{lesson:FA-C470-chador}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a dam, then the Persian for to flow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چادر}}
\textbf{\fa{چادر}} (\emph{châdor}) — \textquotedblleft{}a tent; a chador (a woman's full cloak)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شب} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{چادر} \fa{خوابیدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Shab râ dar châdor khâbidim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We slept in the tent that night.
\end{quote}

Both senses are common; the context tells them apart.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{châdor} comes from Middle Persian \emph{čādur} 'a sheet, a veil', which EtymDB takes from Sanskrit \emph{chattra}: a covering that became both a tent and a cloak.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{châdor}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{châdor}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{châdor}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a dam, then the Persian for to flow, then say \emph{châdor} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کیسه} \fa{خواب} (kise-khâb)}{کیسه خواب (kise-khâb)}]{\fa{کیسه} \fa{خواب} (kise-khâb) — a sleeping bag}

\label{lesson:FA-C470-kise-khab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to flow, then the Persian for a tent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کیسه} \fa{خواب}}
\textbf{\fa{کیسه} \fa{خواب}} (\emph{kise-khâb}) — \textquotedblleft{}a sleeping bag\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شب} \fa{سرد} \fa{بود} \fa{و} \fa{در} \fa{کیسه} \fa{خواب} \fa{لرزیدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Shab sard bud va dar kise-khâb larzidim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The night was cold and we shivered in our sleeping bags.
\end{quote}

\emph{kise} 'bag' + \emph{khâb} 'sleep'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kise-khâb} is a native compound of \emph{kise} 'bag', from Middle Persian \emph{kīsag} (EtymDB), and \emph{khâb} 'sleep', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kise-khâb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kise-khâb}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to flow, then the Persian for a tent, then say \emph{kise-khâb} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هیزم} (hizom)}{هیزم (hizom)}]{\fa{هیزم} (hizom) — firewood}

\label{lesson:FA-C470-hizom}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a tent, then the Persian for a sleeping bag.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هیزم}}
\textbf{\fa{هیزم}} (\emph{hizom}) — \textquotedblleft{}firewood\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{با} \fa{هیزم} \fa{آتش} \fa{روشن} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pedaram bâ hizom âtash roshan kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father lit a fire with firewood.
\end{quote}

\emph{Hizom shekastan} — to chop firewood.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hizom} is a native word, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{ēzm} 'firewood'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گردش} \fa{کردن} (gardesh kardan)}{گردش کردن (gardesh kardan)}]{\fa{گردش} \fa{کردن} (gardesh kardan) — to go for an outing, to stroll, to go sightseeing}

\label{lesson:FA-C470-gardesh-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a sleeping bag, then the Persian for firewood.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گردش} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{گردش} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{gardesh kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to go for an outing, to stroll, to go sightseeing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{عصر} \fa{کنار} \fa{رودخانه} \fa{گردش} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{'Asr kenâr-e rudkhâne gardesh kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the afternoon we went for a stroll by the river.
\end{quote}

\emph{gardesh} 'a turn, an outing' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gardesh kardan} is built from \emph{gardesh} 'a turn, an outing', which EtymDB lists and which is built on \emph{gashtan} 'to turn, to wander', and \emph{kardan} 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اتراق} \fa{کردن} (otrâq kardan)}{اتراق کردن (otrâq kardan)}]{\fa{اتراق} \fa{کردن} (otrâq kardan) — to stop for the night, to camp (on a journey)}

\label{lesson:FA-C470-otraq-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for firewood, then the Persian for to go for an outing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اتراق} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{اتراق} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{otrâq kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to stop for the night, to camp (on a journey)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شب} \fa{کنار} \fa{چشمه} \fa{اتراق} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Shab kenâr-e cheshme otrâq kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At night we camped by the spring.
\end{quote}

\emph{otrâq} 'a halt' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{otrâq kardan} is built from \emph{otrâq} 'a halt, a camp', a loan usually traced to Turkic \emph{otraq} 'a stopping place', and \emph{kardan} 'to do'. EtymDB does not list \emph{otrâq}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for firewood, then the Persian for to go for an outing, then say \emph{otrâq kardan} again
